name: Soul of the Barbarian
body:
Associated Skills: Handle Animal, Intimidate, Knowledge (nature), Survival

Associated Veils: Bloodeater’s Belt, Demon Lord’s Hunger, Gorget of the Stormking, Gorget of the Wyrm, Pit Fiend’s Shroud, Pursuer’s Cuffs, Shaitan’s Earthen Armor, Stone Giant’s Girdle

Rage (Ex)

At 1st level, tapping into the soul of the barbarian allows you to draw from its eternal simmering rage. At 1st level, you can rage for a number of rounds each day equal to 4 + your Wisdom modifier, plus an additional 2 rounds per soulforge level after 1st. Temporary increases to your Wisdom do not increase the number of rounds you can rage per day. You can enter a rage as a free action.

While in rage, you gain a +2 bonus on attack rolls, weapon damage rolls, and Will saving throws. In addition, you take a –2 penalty to Armor Class. You also gain 2 temporary hit points per soulforge level. These temporary hit points are lost first when you take damage, disappear when your rage ends, and are not replenished if you enter a rage again within 1 minute of your previous rage.

While in a rage, you cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skill (except Acrobatics, Fly, Intimidate, and Ride) or any ability that requires patience or concentration (such as spellcasting, or spell-like abilities). You can still use your veils while in this rage, but you still cannot use any spell-like abilities granted by veils.

You can end your rage as a free action and you are fatigued after ending your rage for a number of rounds equal to 2 times the number of rounds spent in the rage.

You cannot enter a new rage while fatigued or exhausted but can otherwise enter rage multiple times during a single encounter or combat. If you fall unconscious, your rage immediately ends.

Fast Movement (Ex)

At 5th level, the soul of the barbarian invigorates you, increasing your base land speed by +10 feet.

Greater Rage (Ex)

At 11th level, your bonus on weapon attack rolls, weapon damage rolls, and Will saves while raging increases by +1. In addition, the amount of temporary hit points gained when entering a rage increases to 3 per soulforge level.

Tireless Rage (Ex)

At 17th level, you are no longer fatigued at the end of your rage.
